title: Ambiguous Rotating Sphere
summary: A sphere made of dots can seem to reverse its rotation.
tryIt: Watch the sphere without focusing on a single dot. Can you perceive either direction?
how: Because the dots provide ambiguous front–back depth information, the same two-dimensional motion can support opposite three-dimensional rotations.

title: Peripheral Drift
summary: Still patterns sometimes appear to swirl.
tryIt: Scan around the image rather than staring at its center.
how: Certain luminance and color arrangements combined with small eye movements can produce apparent motion. The image itself is stationary.

title: Motion Aftereffect
summary: After watching motion, a stationary image may drift the other way.
tryIt: Watch the moving stripes for about 15 seconds, then press Pause and inspect them.
how: Prolonged exposure to motion adapts direction-sensitive visual mechanisms, creating a temporary aftereffect.

title: Wagon-Wheel Effect
summary: A rotating wheel can appear to slow, stop or reverse.
tryIt: Change the wheel speed and watch the spokes.
how: Repeated spoke patterns and temporal sampling can make the apparent rotational direction ambiguous, especially under periodic illumination or video sampling.

title: Necker Cube
summary: A wireframe cube can flip its apparent orientation.
tryIt: Look at the cube. Which of the two square faces is nearest? Try switching it.
how: The drawing omits reliable depth cues, so the brain can organize its edges into two competing three-dimensional interpretations.

title: Rubin’s Vase
summary: Do you see a vase, or two faces?
tryIt: Look at the central white region and then the black regions.
how: The same boundary can be assigned to different figures, changing which region appears to be foreground.

title: Duck–Rabbit
summary: An outline may read as two different animals.
tryIt: Imagine the left side as a bill; then reinterpret it as ears.
how: A single ambiguous outline activates multiple meaningful object interpretations.

title: Spinning Silhouette
summary: A silhouetted figure can seem to change its turning direction.
tryIt: Watch the simplified figure and imagine a reversal.
how: When depth cues are weak, the brain may interpret the silhouette’s rotation in either direction. Not everyone experiences a switch.

title: Simultaneous Contrast
summary: Identical gray patches look different on light and dark backgrounds.
tryIt: Compare the two central gray squares. Use Reveal to check.
how: Surrounding luminance alters how bright an identical central patch appears.

title: Checker Shadow
summary: A shadow alters how light or dark a surface appears.
tryIt: Compare the two marked patches in the demonstration.
how: The visual system estimates surface reflectance while accounting for illumination and context.

title: Color Afterimage
summary: A color may linger after you look away.
tryIt: Fixate on the colored disk, then switch to a pale background.
how: Visual adaptation changes the sensitivity of color-opponent responses, briefly producing complementary afterimages.

title: White’s Illusion
summary: Identical gray sections seem lighter or darker.
tryIt: Compare gray areas embedded in contrasting stripes.
how: Their appearance depends on spatial organization and surrounding luminance; simple local contrast alone does not explain every case.

title: Müller–Lyer Illusion
summary: Arrowheads make equal lines seem different lengths.
tryIt: Decide which horizontal segment is longer, then reveal their endpoints.
how: Arrowhead configurations influence perceived extent, even when the central segments have equal physical lengths.

title: Ponzo Illusion
summary: Parallel perspective cues make equal lines look unequal.
tryIt: Which horizontal bar appears longer?
how: Converging context lines suggest distance, altering the apparent scale of equal image lengths.

title: Ebbinghaus Illusion
summary: Equal circles appear different among larger or smaller circles.
tryIt: Compare the two orange central circles.
how: Surrounding circle sizes and spacing shift the perceived relative size of the center.

title: Café Wall Illusion
summary: Parallel tile rows seem to tilt.
tryIt: Follow the thin dividing lines with your eyes.
how: Staggered high-contrast tiles and mortar lines affect local orientation signals.

title: Kinetic Depth Effect
summary: Moving points reveal a three-dimensional object.
tryIt: Watch the rotating dot cloud and imagine its front and back swapping.
how: Motion supplies information about three-dimensional structure, even when ordinary depth cues are missing.
terms: Kinetic depth effect · structure from motion

title: Hollow-Face Illusion
summary: A concave face may seem convex.
tryIt: Examine the shaded facial mask and compare possible depth interpretations.
how: Strong prior expectations that faces protrude can outweigh inconsistent depth cues.

title: Ames Room
summary: A distorted room can make people look different in size.
tryIt: Inspect the forced-perspective room drawing.
how: A specially shaped room viewed from one point can mimic ordinary rectangular geometry, biasing size judgments.

title: Impossible Trident
summary: The parts fit locally, but not as one coherent object.
tryIt: Trace the prongs from one end to the other.
how: Local depth interpretations conflict when the whole picture is considered.

title: Troxler Fading
summary: Peripheral details may fade while you fixate.
tryIt: Stare at the central cross without moving your gaze for 15–30 seconds.
how: Stable peripheral stimulation can become less noticeable through adaptation and limited eye-motion refresh.

title: Blind Spot
summary: A small mark can disappear from your vision.
tryIt: Close your left eye, stare at the left cross with your right eye, and change viewing distance.
how: The optic disc has no photoreceptors; the visual system fills in the missing region.

title: Motion-Induced Blindness
summary: Stationary targets may intermittently vanish among moving dots.
tryIt: Fixate at the center while attending to the colored target.
how: A moving visual surround can suppress awareness of otherwise visible stationary targets.

title: Change Blindness
summary: Even large changes can escape notice.
tryIt: Watch two scenes alternate with a blank interval and try to detect what changes.
how: Interruptions can prevent reliable comparison between successive scenes, especially without focused attention.
